title: catalyst-requests-lab-notes-sep-2025
body:
Purpose:
Quick, evidence-led compilation of customer feedback micro-asks surfaced in July–Sep 2025 field work. Aim: create a short experimentable ledger of small-to-medium tasks that (a) unblock customers fast, (b) validate impact, and (c) feed product backlog with proximate implementation paths.

How to read this doc: each row below is a compact synthesis: customer quote (if available), observed frequency / strength, hypothesized root cause, low-effort probe or mitigation, suggested owner, and escalation notes (risk / blockers). Prioritization uses Impact (H/M/L) x Effort (S/M/L).

Summary findings (headline):
- Dominant themes: routing/fallback predictability, per-route cost visibility, and embedding stability for small-batch workloads.
- Many asks are incremental (non-architectural) and can be validated by config toggles / feature flags within 2–6 weeks.
- Two higher-risk items (private deployment onboarding friction; KV cache corruption in Llama-2 7B quantized path) require engineering deep-dive; flagged separately.

Compact ledger (short form):
1) "Prefer deterministic fallback model rather than implicit choice" — multiple enterprise customers
   - Frequency / strength: 18 conversations, 7 labeled urgent by AE.
   - Hypothesis: current smart-routing default switches models when latency spikes; customers interpret silent swap as output change.
   - Proposed probe: add visible response header and SDK event "fallback_used" + opt-in deterministic fallback policy (prefer cheaper variant vs prefer stable variant).
   - Owner: Product-hosted-api + SDK (Tomas Berg).
   - Impact/Effort: H / S (feature-flag + header + docs).
   - Escalation: link to Support thread: JIRA-CS-1127.

2) "Token cost breakdown per route in console is unclear for multi-model chains" — mid-market PLG user
   - Frequency: 6 tickets, 3 product calls.
   - Hypothesis: console aggregates tokens at top level; users want per-step token and per-model estimation for canary runs.
   - Probe: expose per-route token estimate in Run UI and exportable CSV; quick mock in Console staging.
   - Owner: Console/observability (Evelyn Chen).
   - Impact/Effort: M / S.

3) "Embeddings drift across quantization profiles for small-batch inference" — AI-native startup
   - Frequency: observed in bench tests + 2 customer-reported regressions.
   - Hypothesis: quantization profile selection heuristics are too coarse for <32 batch sizes; fallback to full-precision recommended but not surfaced.
   - Probe: runtime toggle to force fp16 embeddings for low-batch flows, with telemetry event. A/B test with 10 customers.
   - Owner: Serving-runtime + Applied-ML (Omar Ruiz).
   - Impact/Effort: H / M.
   - Notes: potential cost increase; include cost impact estimate in probe.

4) "Private deployment onboarding: opaque preflight checks and long certificate cycles" — regulated customer
   - Frequency: 4 enterprise deals stalled.
   - Hypothesis: onboarding checklist assumes infra expertise not present in some customers; cert rotation docs are incomplete.
   - Probe: create a condensed "Kickstart" script + one-click cert rotation guide and sample terraform module. Pilot with 1 customer.
   - Owner: Private-deployments + Solutions-eng (Priya Nair).
   - Impact/Effort: H / M-L (documentation + small infra templates).
   - Escalation: consider professional services offering as short-term bypass.

5) "Timeouts during burst traffic lead to silent partial outputs" — two PLG customers
   - Frequency: intermittent, tied to cold-starts during bursts.
   - Hypothesis: autoscale reactive policy default too conservative for certain pipelines; partial-response behavior confusing.
   - Probe: experiment with conservative warm-pool size and fallback streaming behavior that sends an explicit 'incomplete' flag to SDKs.
   - Owner: Dedicated + SRE (team: eng-serving-runtime).
   - Impact/Effort: M / M.

6) "Better prompt history sizing UI and default policy for chat sessions" — several product teams
   - Frequency: product design feedback + 3 pilot customers.
   - Hypothesis: default history retention/pinning not aligned with cost-conscious users.
   - Probe: add per-session retention presets: minimal/standard/full with visible token preview. A small UX experiment.
   - Owner: Product-hosted-api + DevX.
   - Impact/Effort: M / S.

7) Low-effort quick wins (can be shipped in 1–2 sprints):
   - a) Add "fallback_used" header and SDK event (see item 1).
   - b) Console: per-route token export (item 2).
   - c) Quick onboarding checklist for Private (item 4).
   - Owners suggested: Tomas / Evelyn / Priya.

Risk flags and unknowns:
- KV cache corruption (edge-case) reported with Llama-2 7B quantized path: low frequency but high severity if it manifests in production. Request: SRE & Applied-ML forensic log collection. (Linked: JIRA-FEAT-2043).
- Data residency concern: some APAC customers ask for clearer mapping of where caches and logs live. Escalate to security/compliance for templated language.

Suggested experiments & metrics (how we validate):
- For each probe, collect: success metric (reduction in ticket reopen rate or explicit customer satisfaction), telemetry events (opt-in metrics for fallbacks, quant profile used), cost delta (estimated tokens/cost change), and time-to-first-fix.
- Target: move 60% of triaged micro-asks into either "quick-win" or "A/B probe" within 6 weeks.

Next actions (this doc owner):
- Week 0: Review with product leads (scheduled sync 2025-10-06).
- Week 1: Create 1-pagers for items 1–3 and land feature flags for fallback headers.
- Week 2–4: Run two small A/B probes (embeddings fp16 toggle, console export).
- Week 3: Kickstart private-deployments checklist pilot with one partner.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we prefer a single "fallback preference" policy or multiple discrete flags? (Product tradeoff: simplicity vs control).
- Should embeddings low-batch default to fp16 at runtime or be an explicit customer opt-in?

Appendix — raw customer notes (anonymized):
- "We had a client demo where the model answer changed mid-demo. No one on the call knew why — looked like a regression." — Financial services pilot.
- "When we run batch of 12 for embeddings, quality drops sometimes compared to our baseline. We had to re-encode." — Search startup.
- "Private install took three infra cycles because cert rotation failed once; we needed the vendor team to step in." — Healthtech regulated buyer.

If you want to reuse: this doc is intentionally compact. For a fuller report, I can expand the appendices with evidence counts, transcribed quotes, and a proposed roadmap slice for Q4.

Maya Thompson
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Internal note: drop into cs-voice-lab and tag relevant owners after review.
